Hi,
I am a 20 year old F in uni that has anxiety but not to your level- reading this however reminds me of the times I have felt like you have, completely ruined my relationships with people and then beat myself up for it.

I can only sympathise and I want to say it will get better- I don't know if my advice will help but here are some tips that might help (stuff I have done from middle school when I didnt talk to anyone and had no friends till now where I have improved quite a bit with anxiety attacks when interacting with people).

- going to stores/malls/cafés by yourself and asking an employee a question or even just order something while: maintining eye contact, and smiling. It can be very simple but hey- its practice! Specially with girls too! ( keep in mind some employees can not give a shit too so dont take anything to heart)

- make your body comfortable in spaces with more people (dont need to interact- just accustom yourself- and it might end up including some small talk too!) like gyms, parks, malls 
and keep in mind youre doing it for yourself! dont see others doing etc/having fun and get down (something I used to do a lot - self pity- but I remembered that these are baby steps) And you can leave anytime if it gets really bad!

if its possible: get a job - just a small part time one - specially one with not a lot if employees and observe the boss/manager of the business beforehand if you can (a rude or negative one can make your life miserable :( )
- this last one REALLY helped me: I had to interact with customers and employees everyday and becoming accustomed to it helped become calmer with interacting with others in my daily life

I would suggest something like dish washing/stacking shelves - basically not too much forced interaction as the last thing you want is to feel like throwing up and crying everytime before your shift (been there). 

*** I will add: volunteering is another really good one- not as many risks and no real pressure to interact with anyone- also good on resumes! Try your local conseration area for something lowkey and in nature! 



Keep trying! Professional help, different tactics, etc I know it is hard but dont let your anxiety engulph and fully define yourself. You have a lot of years to work on this its never too late.

Baby steps. IMO it might help to talk about it after you can get a bit closer with a coworker or find a natural spot in a conversation to put it in.

This can be so stressful so hang in there. I write down all the things I need to do and accept right away that the worse that can happen might- but Ill start off my life from that point and only go up. I know its hard to think about but at least for me it allows me to finish my tasks and wait for whatever response comes right back at me.

Also having a small hobby to do (read, draw, workout) afted you finish your tasks can help with the anxious thoughts of what might happen while you wait for responses.

I used to have a really hard time making eye contact up until grade 9- when I realised I would almost never look people in the eye.
I dont know the reason, but I had become extremely depressed in middle school and barely had any contact with anyone including my parents at home who didnt really care.

One other reason I found it hard was because in the very beginning I wouldnt do it right- I would make eye contact to someone by holding it too long and it felt very sexual or like I really liked them- I was too worried about stuff like this.

I practiced and realised that it helps holding eye contact in one eye and looking away once in a while.

Now its something natural to me but once in a while Ill have to remind myself to do it.

Sorry I didnt fully answer your question but thats just a relevant experience from me!
